newsitem.title: USA: Plains feedlot cattle bid $72, no sales - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains feedlot cattle bid $72, no sales - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle markets were quiet early Monday, with no sales of slaughter steers or heifers reported, feedlot sources said.
Packers were bidding $72.00 per cwt, steady with last week's top, while owners were pricing cattle at $74.00.
Sales were not expected to occur until Thursday as packers have plenty of cattle inventory following last week's record-large sales at 196,000 head in the Panhandle area.
Most feedlots sold out their showlists last week resulting in light, if any, carryover into this week's showlists, which were expected to be seven to eight percent smaller, they said.
Some cattle feeders said they expect cattle to trade at $73.00 once sales resurface because of tight finished cattle supplies and expectations for continued strong beef demand.
Beef clearance at retail meat counters reportedly was strong over the weekend and retailers will be looking to restock their coolers, market sources said.
Boxed beef prices Friday were quoted up $0.05 to $0.24 per cwt for choice cuts and down $0.17 to $0.26 for select grade cuts, on 257 fabricated loads reported sold, according to USDA.
